item.title: Wind–solar generation and scarcity resilience are spatially decoupled in Europe
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04191-7

Mean generation and resilience to continent-wide wind and solar scarcity differ spatially, with several moderate-resource regions maintaining generation better than high-resource regions, according to analysis of daily wind and solar output across 128,931 European wind turbine locations from 1986-2025.
item.dc:title: Wind–solar generation and scarcity resilience are spatially decoupled in Europe
item.dc:creator: Dirk Schindler
Christopher Jung

item.title: Two large unstable slopes in West Greenland illustrates an emerging Arctic tsunami hazard
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04175-7

Newly identified unstable slopes in central West Greenland highlight the emerging Arctic hazard from landslide-generated tsunamis, potentially linked to ongoing permafrost thaw, according to field observations, remote sensing and numerical modelling analysis.
item.dc:title: Two large unstable slopes in West Greenland illustrates an emerging Arctic tsunami hazard
item.dc:creator: Marie Keiding
Finn Løvholt
Sylfest Glimsdal

item.title: Pathways to pyrite through polysulfides and metastable iron sulfides in marine sediments
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04161-z

Polysulfides facilitate the transformation of nanoparticulate Fe-S phases into pyrite in natural sediments, providing new insight into early diagenetic pyrite formation, according to spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis.
item.dc:title: Pathways to pyrite through polysulfides and metastable iron sulfides in marine sediments
item.dc:creator: Maria C. Figueroa
Ravi K. Kukkadapu
Daniel D. Gregory
Anthony Chappaz
Mark H. Engelhard
Timothy W. Lyons

item.title: Phototroph-specific nitrogen isotopes detail N<sub>2</sub>-fixation increases at the end-Triassic extinction
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04159-7

“Primary producer-specific nitrogen isotopes indicate a substantial reorganization of the coastal nitrogen cycle following the end-Triassic mass extinction; analyzed using compound-specific nitrogen and carbon isotopes of sedimentary metalloporphyrins derived from phototrophs at St. Audrie’s Bay, UK”
